questions.q: DKD develops in what share of diabetic patients?
questions.exp: RISK: 50-60% of diabetic patients; ↑ with age. (Book p815)

questions.q: The risk of DKD rises with age.
questions.exp: ↑ with age. (Book p815)

questions.q: Match the following diabetes type to its screening timing — 1) Type 1 DM  2) Type 2 DM  3) The screening test … A) At diagnosis  B) Screen 5 yearly  C) Check for albuminuria
questions.exp: T1 DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) — screen 5 yearly; T2 DM — screen at diagnosis; screening = check for albuminuria. (Book p815)

questions.q: Albuminuria screening is repeated every:
questions.exp: Check for albuminuria (3-6 months). (Book p815)

questions.q: The 'superior, but cumbersome' screening test is:
questions.exp: 24 urine protein (superior, but cumbersome). (Book p815)

questions.q: The routine screening test named is:
opts: Serum cystatin C at each visit
questions.exp: Early morning albumin: creatinine (ACR). (Book p815)

questions.q: Match the following ACR level to its label — 1) <30 mg/g  2) 30-300 mg/g  3) >300 mg/g … A) Albuminuria  B) Normal  C) Microalbuminuria
questions.exp: Levels: <30 normal; 30-300 microalbuminuria (endothelial injury): ↑ risk for thrombosis; >300 albuminuria. (Book p815)

questions.q: The microalbuminuria band runs from 30 mg/g to:
questions.exp: 30-300 mg/g: microalbuminuria. (Book p815)

questions.q: Microalbuminuria marks endothelial injury with a raised thrombosis risk.
questions.exp: Microalbuminuria (endothelial injury): ↑ risk for thrombosis. (Book p815)

questions.q: A newly diagnosed type 2 diabetic patient is booked for DKD screening. When should the first check happen?
questions.exp: T2 DM: screen at diagnosis. (Book p815)

questions.q: The first pathogenic step of DKD is:
opts: Tubular atrophy with secondary interstitial scarring
Afferent arterial vasodilation + efferent arterial vasoconstriction
Efferent arteriolar vasodilation alone, without afferent change
Glomerular ischemia with low filtration pressure
questions.exp: Pathogenesis: afferent arterial vasodilation + efferent arterial vasoconstriction → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension. (Book p815)

questions.q: Match the following factor to the arteriolar tone it drives — 1) NO bioavailability  2) Prostaglandins  3) Angiotensin II  4) Thromboxane A2 … A) Net ↓ afferent arteriolar resistance  B) Net ↑ efferent arteriolar resistance
questions.exp: Net ↓ afferent resistance: NO bioavailability, prostaglandins, kallikrein-kinins, atrial natriuretic factor, angiotensin (↓). Net ↑ efferent resistance: angiotensin II, thromboxane A2, endothelin-1 (ETA receptor). (Book p815)

questions.q: All but one are listed as causing a net reduction of afferent arteriolar resistance. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Afferent list: NO bioavailability, prostaglandins, kallikrein-kinins, atrial natriuretic factor, angiotensin (↓); thromboxane A2 is on the efferent list. (Book p815)

questions.q: The factors causing a net increase of efferent arteriolar resistance are:
questions.exp: Efferent list: angiotensin II, thromboxane A2, endothelin-1 (ETA receptor). (Book p815)

questions.q: Endothelin-1 drives efferent arteriolar resistance through the ETA receptor.
opts: False — it acts via the ETB receptor
False — it acts on the macula densa
True, but only in type 1 DM
questions.exp: Endothelin-1 (ETA receptor) is on the efferent list. (Book p815)

questions.q: The net result of the tone changes in DKD is:
questions.exp: … → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension. (Book p815)

questions.q: In normal physiology (panel A), the afferent tone is:
opts: Fixed, with no TGF at all
Appropriate, with normal TGF and normal GFR
questions.exp: A — normal physiology: normal TGF, normal GFR, appropriate afferent arterial tone. (Book p815)

questions.q: In early diabetic nephropathy (panel B), the defect is:
opts: Afferent vasodilation + increased Na/glucose reabsorption → ↓ Na delivery to macula densa
Efferent dilation with increased Na delivery to the macula densa
Macula densa hyperplasia with fixed TGF
questions.exp: B — hyperfiltration in early stages: afferent arterial vasodilation, increased Na/glucose reabsorption, decreased Na⁺ delivery to macula densa → impaired TGF, elevated GFR. (Book p815)

questions.q: SGLT2 inhibition (panel C) restores the TGF because it:
opts: Lowers Na⁺ delivery to the macula densa via enhanced reabsorption
Blocks the macula densa sensing entirely
Raises Na⁺ delivery to the macula densa via reduced proximal reabsorption
questions.exp: C — SGLT-2 inhibition in proximal tubule → increased Na⁺ delivery to macula densa → afferent arterial constriction → normalization of GFR; glucosuria. (Book p815)

questions.q: Fill up: SGLT2 inhibitors raise Na⁺ entry to the ______, constricting the afferent arteriole.
questions.exp: ↑ Na⁺ entry to macula densa → afferent arteriole constriction → ↓ GFR → ↓ hyperfiltration injury. (Book p815)

questions.q: SGLT2 inhibitors are the 1st line management for hyperfiltration injury.
opts: False — they are for hypertension only
True, but only in type 1 DM
questions.exp: SGLT2 (-): 1st line management. (Book p815)

questions.q: A diabetic with early nephropathy has an elevated GFR from afferent vasodilation. The mechanism by which an SGLT2 inhibitor normalizes the GFR is:
opts: Suppression of renin release alone, without TGF
Osmotic diuresis from the induced glucosuria
Increased Na⁺ delivery to the macula densa → afferent constriction
Direct dilation of the efferent arteriole, with no TGF change
questions.exp: SGLT-2 inhibition → increased Na⁺ delivery to macula densa → afferent arteriole constriction → normalization of GFR. (Book p815)

questions.exp: Diagram labels: afferent arteriole, efferent arteriole, macula densa, juxtaglomerular cells, podocyte, proximal tubule. (Book p815)

questions.exp: KW lesions - Kimmelstiel wilson. (Book p816)

questions.q: All but one are Traver classes. Which is the odd one out?

Isolated microscopic hematuria, sediment otherwise inactive

units.title: Risk and albuminuria screening
units.guide: RISK: 50-60% of diabetic patients, ↑ with age; T1 DM screen 5 yearly, T2 DM at diagnosis. Screening: check for albuminuria every 3-6 months — 24-hr urine protein (superior, but cumbersome) or early morning albumin:creatinine (ACR). Levels: <30 normal; 30-300 microalbuminuria (endothelial injury, ↑ thrombosis risk); >300 albuminuria.

units.title: Hyperfiltration pathogenesis and the SGLT2i mechanism
units.guide: Afferent vasodilation + efferent vasoconstriction → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension. Net ↓ afferent resistance: NO bioavailability, prostaglandins, kallikrein-kinins, ANF, angiotensin (↓); net ↑ efferent resistance: angiotensin II, thromboxane A2, endothelin-1 (ETA). Panels: A normal (appropriate tone, normal TGF/GFR); B early DN (afferent vasodilation + ↑ Na/glucose reabsorption → ↓ Na delivery to macula densa → impaired TGF); C SGLT2i (proximal Na reabsorption ↓ → ↑ Na to macula densa → afferent constriction → GFR normalized; glucosuria). SGLT2i: 1st line for hyperfiltration injury.

units.title: Mogensen staging (T1 DM model)
units.guide: Mogensen: on the model of T1 DM; not very accurate for T2 DM; stage V = ESRD. Table: I hyperfiltration (GFR ↑, BP =/↑); II silent + microalbuminuria (GFR ↓/↑, BP ↑ — 24-hr ambulatory monitoring: absence of nocturnal dipping, wide pulse pressure); III macroalbuminuria (GFR =/↓, BP ↑↑); IV renal impairment (GFR ↓, BP ↑↑↑).

units.title: Traver histology, nodular diseases and DN criteria
units.guide: Traver et al: histological; characteristic pattern nodular glomerulosclerosis. I GBM thickening (earliest); II mesangial expansion (m/c 90%; afferent & efferent hyalinosis); III nodular sclerosis — KW lesions (Kimmelstiel wilson), only 50% pts, most specific; IV advanced diabetic glomerulosclerosis. Nodular kidney diseases: diabetes (KW nodules), MPGN, lichen deposition diseases, amyloidosis, smokers. Diabetic nephropathy = albuminuric DKD; criteria (all of): proteinuria (albuminuria) nephrotic range without syndrome; no micro/macro hematuria.

units.title: DN criteria continued, non-albuminuric DKD and NDRD red flags
units.guide: Criteria continue: hypertension; edema extra > intravascular d/t Na⁺, glucose transporters; retinopathy concordance T1 100%, T2 65%; if any absent → biopsy. Non-albuminuric DKD: tubulointerstitial & vascular damage. Non-diabetic RPD: nephrotic syndrome; renal dysfunction onset <10y of DM (T1 > T2); absent nephropathy (T1 > T2); mx biopsy; hematuria/RBC casts; extra-renal vasculitis, myeloma; RPRF. Hypertension in DKD diagram: exogenous + genetic → obesity ↔ T2DM → insulin resistance/hyperleptinemia, hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia → sympathetic activation, micro/macrovasculopathy → angiotensin II → hypertension.

units.title: Management: glucose target, DM drug table, proteinuria control
units.guide: Target glucose >7 mg/dl as printed (to avoid hypoglycemia). DM control & weight loss: lifestyle; DOC metformin if GFR >30 ml/min. Macrovascular (CKD/ASCVD): DOC SGLT2i — canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin; initiated GFR >30. Table: metformin neutral/neutral-potential benefit/high/low/neutral; SGLT2i benefit/benefit/benefit/intermediate/low/loss; GLP-1 benefit/benefit/potential benefit/high/low/loss; DPP-4 neutral/neutral/potential risk (saxagliptin)/intermediate/low/neutral; insulin neutral/neutral/neutral/highest/high/gain; sulfonylureas neutral/high/high/gain; TZD neutral/potential benefit (pioglitazone)/increased risk/high/low/gain; α-glucosidase inhibitors neutral/neutral/neutral/intermediate/low/neutral. Proteinuria: 1st line SGLT2i + ACEi; 2nd line finerenone (non-steroidal MRA) — monitor s. K⁺ (hyperkalemia risk).

units.title: Other DM drugs in CKD: preferred agents and eGFRD-safe list
units.sec: Other DM drugs in CKD · p818
units.guide: GLP-1 RA: most preferred liraglutide; oral semaglutide; no dose adjustment. DPP-4: most preferred linagliptin (no dose adjustment); others require adjustment. Sulfonylureas: not preferred; renal safe glipizide, gliclazide. Drugs safe in eGFRD: insulin; glipizide, gliclazide; imeglimin (CKD) = oxidative phosphorylation blocker.
